title: Engineering Manager - Software and System Testing (f/m/d)
description:
About Munich Electrification

Munich Electrification is an innovative company founded with the aim of accelerating the transition to electric and connected mobility. We develop innovative electronic control units for electric vehicles and stationary storage systems for our global customers. Our international team is composed of highly motivated and exceptional engineers. As a small and specialized team we are well-aware of the importance of each individual colleague and support and promote each employee according to their abilities and needs. Our office with adjacent prototype and testing lab is located in the heart of Munich at the Heimeranplatz.

This is what we stand for:

- Technological Leadership: We challenge norms, innovate quickly, and anticipate future needs. We take smart risks and learn from outcomes to stay ahead.

- Sustainability: We actively drive change for a sustainable future, aware of our impact and inspiring others to build a better world.

- Team Culture: We believe work should be enjoyable, fostering a spirit of inspiration, celebration, and teamwork across the globe.

- Entrepreneurial Spirit: We embrace change, think big, and push limits with passion.

Your Role

As an Engineering Manager within our Testing department, you will be the driving force behind the quality and reliability of our innovative software for Electronic Control Units (ECUs) in the energy storage and electric car sectors. You will lead and mentor a dedicated team of test engineers, taking ultimate responsibility for our overall product quality, test strategy, and process compliance as well as the strategic planning, hiring, and team building of your team. Your strong leadership will be instrumental in building a world-class testing organization and ensuring our products meet the highest standards of safety and excellence, making a significant impact on the future of electric energy storage technology.

As part of your role, you will:

Lead, Empower, and Develop Your Team

  • Take full personnel responsibility for your team, including hiring, onboarding, professional development, and compensation planning.

  • Act as the primary "Go-To" person and mentor, supporting team members to achieve their goals and grow personally and professionally.

  • Foster a collaborative and innovative team environment, facilitating exchange and knowledge sharing.

  • Monitor team workload and health, manage headcount planning, and structure teams for maximum effectiveness and well-being.

    Own Product Quality and Test Delivery

  • Hold the overall delivery responsibility for the testing processes of the product groups under your supervision.

  • Enable and empower the team to constantly innovate and enhance our test automation frameworks and infrastructure.

  • Make sure the test strategy and efforts are aligned with the product roadmap and customer needs.

    Drive Process Excellence and Compliance:

  • Ensure team compliance with critical automotive processes and norms such as ISO 26262, ISO 21434, and ASPICE.

  • Serve as the primary escalation point for any process, quality, or technical concerns from the team.

  • Act as a direct interface for Product and Project Management, Systems and Software Development leadership, and HR to align on strategies and ensure seamless collaboration.

Your Profile

Educational Foundation: Successfully completed university degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a comparable engineering field.

Professional Experience:

  • More than 5 years of professional experience in software quality assurance, validation, or testing, preferably in an automotive embedded systems environment.

  • More than 3 years of experience in a technical leadership, test architecture, or management role, with a proven track record of leading testing efforts for complex products.

  • Demonstrable experience with test automation strategies, tools, and frameworks.

    Domain and Standards Expertise:

  • Deep understanding of quality and safety-critical standards, ideally with hands-on experience applying ISO 26262 and ASPICE in a testing context.

  • Experience in the field of high-voltage (HV) batteries, ECUs, or battery management systems is a significant plus.

  • Familiarity with automotive cybersecurity (ISO 21434) is highly desirable.

    Leadership Qualities:

The role

Seccl is growing fast, and so is the opportunity to make better use of our data. Our Data Engineering team has built strong foundations for reliable, scalable data delivery, and we’re now expanding our capabilities to make that data more accessible, actionable, and valuable to our teams and clients.

As a Data Analytics Engineer, you’ll sit at the intersection of data engineering and analytics. You’ll use strong software engineering and data modelling practices to develop production-quality datasets, while working closely with stakeholders to understand how data can help solve real business problems.

You’ll also help us evolve how data moves through our platform, including opportunities to work with streaming and event-driven technologies as we move towards more timely and incremental data processing.

 

On a typical day you will be…

  • Designing, building, and maintaining robust data models using SQL and DBT, transforming complex source data into clear, reusable datasets for analytics and downstream consumers

  • Working with Product managers, Engineers, Operations, and client-facing teams to understand requirements, clarify business logic, and translate problems into scalable data solutions

  • Helping define and maintain consistent metrics, modelling standards, and analytical best practices across the business

  • Supporting our journey towards more real-time and incremental data processing, including working with technologies such as MongoDB change streams, Kafka, and AWS MSK

  • Helping teams become more self-sufficient with data by making datasets understandable, well documented, and easy to consume

You’ll be successful in this role if you…

  • Have strong SQL and data modelling skills and are comfortable transforming large, complex datasets into reliable, reusable analytical models

  • Have experience with Python and modern analytics engineering tooling such as DBT, including testing, documentation, version control, and CI/CD practices

  • Are familiar with both relational and non-relational database architecture

  • Understand dimensional modelling and how to design datasets that are intuitive and effective for analytics, BI, and downstream data products

  • Have experience working with cloud data platforms and services, ideally within AWS

  • Ideally have experience with event-driven or streaming data architectures, particularly Kafka/AWS MSK, MongoDB change streams, CDC, or similar technologies

  • Have hands on experience working with an orchestration tool such as Airflow

  • Thrive in cross-functional collaboration, working effectively with Product managers, Engineers, Operations, analysts, and client facing teams

  • Communicate clearly and can explain technical concepts and trade-offs to both technical and non-technical audiences

  • Take ownership of problems end-to-end, from understanding the requirement and designing the solution through to implementation, validation, documentation, and adoption

This role isn’t for you if:

  • You rely on heavily on top-down direction. Here, you’ll have a freedom and ownership early on – it’s up to you to shape your growth and deliver outcomes

  • You’re uncomfortable in a fast-paced environment. Our ability to move quickly and scale effectively is key to our success – we need people who can adapt and think on their feet

  • You struggle to follow through on ideas. We value people who not only think big, but also deliver

  • You resist change. We’re growing quickly, and the environment can be ambiguous – you’ll thrive here if you see change as an opportunity rather than a hurdle

What’s in it for you…

This is the senior computer vision engineering authority for Hawk-Eye's tracking technology, and it is an individual contributor role.

Our tracking sits underneath almost everything Hawk-Eye sells. Goal-line technology, semi-automated offside, electronic line calling, automated ball-strike. Live and post-game data. You would be the person who decides how that is built. The role carries two hats. As Software Architect you own the software-level architectural design across tracking, auto-officiating and data delivery. As computer vision authority you lead the core domains: camera calibration, ball tracking, skeletal tracking, and the R&D that feeds them.

It is a hands-on job. You set architecture for new tracking problems as they arrive, you safeguard the shared frameworks, and when a live delivery is at risk you are the escalation point who gets into the code.

What you would own

Architecture across the value stream. You are the lead architect for every tracking and auto-officiating product in T&AO. You set the initial architecture when a new tracking problem enters the business, run the Software Domain Owner model so shared libraries like calibration have named codeowners, and keep designs consistent across sports. You represent tracking in the Engineering Architecture Steering group and feed into architecture conversations across Hawk-Eye and the wider Sony Sports organisation.

Part of that is judgement about reuse. Keeping value streams on a common tracking codebase pays off until it doesn't, and knowing where that line sits is the job.

Computer vision direction. You are the subject matter authority. You decide where our vision processing and ML integration goes next, research new tracking technologies and bring them in, and build prototypes when a proposal needs proving rather than describing.

Modern tooling, properly evaluated. We want agentic coding frameworks, LLM-driven development tools and automated code generation working inside heavy C++ and Python codebases, with guidelines that hold up. You would lead that adoption and decide what earns its place.

Growing other engineers. You coach the Squad Tech Leads, guide junior architects, and run CV Algorithm talks, HawkTalks and tutorials. You also help us hire well, including technical assessment for CV and ML roles.

The awkward bits. Operational health of ML training and synthetic data infrastructure sits with you, including escalating the gaps in ownership and support with options attached.

What we are looking for

The core of it is deep multi-camera computer vision. Camera calibration including intrinsics, extrinsics, distortion models, anti-wobble and bundle adjustment. Triangulation. 3D ball and pose estimation, skeletal tracking, continuous-time modelling, inverse kinematics.

On top of that:

  • Expert cross-platform C++ across Windows and Linux, x86 and ARM, with CMake and real performance profiling ability

  • Strong working knowledge of GPU inference (TensorRT, Triton) and ML pipelines (PyTorch, ONNX)

  • Proven experience running tracking at scale in AWS, on-premise and on edge devices

  • Hands-on use of AI coding agents and LLM orchestration to accelerate algorithm R&D and refactoring in large codebases

  • A working understanding of generative AI, synthetic data generation and where they genuinely help real-time CV

The parts that are harder to put in a bullet point. You can set architecture across many squads and sports and make pragmatic calls on reuse, cost and time to market. You write clearly: design documents, proposals with options, explanations a non-technical stakeholder can follow. You are comfortable in front of external engineering partners, which here means Sony, NVIDIA and AWS alongside sports leagues and federations. And you can size work honestly, state your confidence in it, and say what we should stop or delay.

What this role is not

Worth being direct about, because senior CV engineers are usually offered the other thing.

This is not a people management role. Nobody reports to you. Line management sits elsewhere and we are not planning to move it.

It is not project or delivery management either. Delivery Leads coordinate squad delivery across T&AO. You own technical direction and escalation, not sprint management.

You are not a Product Owner. Product sets the market and problem priorities, you work with them to define the solution.

You are not a Squad Tech Lead. Day-to-day technical leadership of squads sits with the Squad Tech Leads and Engineering Leads. You mentor them and step in on the complex and high-risk problems.

And you are not a gatekeeper for other value streams. You give them alignment and access to shared tracking IP. You do not own their roadmaps.
